I have read the test file and both relevant source files. Now I can judge.

**Finding 1 judgment:**

The quoted code is at lines 355–359 of `plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/tests/claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh`:

```
cat > "$ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE/$_dscla4_issue/run-status-comment.txt" <<'RSCEOF'
<!-- zbuild-run-status run_id=holder-run-99 -->
<!-- zbuild-holder: run-holder-99 on machine-other -->
run is in progress...
RSCEOF
```

The fixture is hand-written. `rsc_render_header` (line 308 of `scripts/lib/run-status-render.sh`) writes the holder line as:

```bash
[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER:-}" ]] && printf '<!-- zbuild-holder: %s -->\n' "$_ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER"
```

The hand-written fixture's holder content is `run-holder-99 on machine-other`, using an `on` separator that does not reflect any format `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER` actually takes: in production it is `run_id=X machine=Y` (local) or a CI URL (confirmed by the DSCLA-2 sub-test at lines 245–252). The test at lines 377–382 then checks that `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER` contains `run-holder-99` after `zbuild_claim_acquire` reads back the fixture — validating that `_ccgl_read_holder`'s regex parsed the hand-written string, not any string that `rsc_render_header` would actually produce. If `rsc_render_header` changed the comment format (renamed the attribute, altered delimiters, changed spacing), `_ccgl_read_holder`'s regex in production would stop matching, but this test would continue to pass against its frozen fixture. The CLAUDE.md rule is unambiguous: "Data another part of the engine writes is checked against its writer." There is nothing in the test or in the other files that closes this gap.
